open_points.subject: credential echo detection in oversized service responses
open_points.text: “A service's own answer body that echoes one verbatim is withheld from everyone, the owner included” contradicts “Every body as read, whatever its status — reading stops at the ceiling — is searched” when the credential occurs after `service_response_bytes_max`.
open_points.question: Must the kernel continue consuming an oversized response solely to search the entire body for the credential, or does the withholding guarantee cover only the prefix read up to the ceiling?
options: Search only the prefix read up to `service_response_bytes_max`.
Continue reading and searching the entire body without retaining or interpreting bytes beyond the ceiling.
Abort at the ceiling and classify the body as oversized without claiming whether it echoed the credential.
open_points.default_guess: Search only the prefix read up to `service_response_bytes_max`, because A09 explicitly says reading stops at the ceiling.

open_points.subject: agent direct service access versus exclusive personal-data readership
open_points.text: “Owner — ... is the only reader of personal data” conflicts with “An agent's own access to a service — as for processing a photo (decision 17) — is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel” and “the agent processes a photo itself ... with its own access to the service that holds the photo”.
open_points.question: Is the statement that the owner is the only reader of personal data limited to values returned through the kernel surface, or must direct service access also prevent agents from reading service data classified as personal data?
options: The exclusivity applies only to the kernel surface; direct service access is governed outside the kernel.
The exclusivity applies platform-wide, so direct agent access must not expose personal data.
Direct access may expose personal data only for the specifically mentioned photo-processing case.
open_points.default_guess: Limit the personal-data readership promise to the kernel surface, following the new explicit statement that K-14 covers what the kernel itself returns.
